# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | purple | red | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My only outgoing channel is gesture, and it lands on Deaf alone. Deaf can see the bomb but not hear; Deaf *can* speak, and I can hear — so the workable pipeline is: Deaf reads the bomb aloud to me, I look up the answer in my manual, and I gesture the answer back for Deaf to relay to the Blind, who alone can cut.

The bootstrap problem: Deaf and I share no code yet. I can't define one in words, so I open with the most iconic sequence I can — greeting, cooperation, "I am holding written instructions" (my manual), then a request aimed at Deaf ("you — give — please"), meaning: describe what you see, propose how we'll signal. Deaf speaks next in the round order, so whatever convention Deaf announces, I'll hear at the start of round 2 and can then answer with something transparent like repeated identical gestures as counts. I deliberately do not try to transmit the whole 25-cell table — without an agreed enumeration it would be pure noise. One exchange to align, then data.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝", "🤲", "✍", "🫵", "🫴", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | purple | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | yellow | orange | green | purple | red |
| 5 | red | purple | orange | yellow | green |
| 6 | green | yellow | red | orange | purple |
| 8 | green | purple | orange | red | yellow |
| 9 | yellow | green | red | purple | orange |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking, hands report: the bomb holds exactly one display, one light, and five wires at positions one through five. Nothing else I can feel, and no marking or colour reaches me on any of it. Remember the wiring of this room: Mute cannot reach me directly, because gestures never reach me and Mute has no voice. Deaf is my only incoming voice. So: pick the manual pages that match this inventory, gesture your questions to Deaf, and have Deaf speak the answers aloud — wire colours by position, whatever the display shows, whether the light is lit and its colour, plus any printed labels Deaf can see. My hands stay still until a cut comes to me through Deaf's mouth or through you. Deaf's words this round only reach me next round, so the sooner Deaf speaks the visuals, the sooner I can act.
Deaf says: Report from Deaf. The display shows 6. The light is red. There are five wires, and I will list them in order. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is purple. Wire 3 is orange. Wire 4 is green. Wire 5 is yellow. That is everything visible on the bomb. Mute: I understood your signs, and this is the full report. Read the manual and tell Blind, out loud, what to do with a display of 6, a red light, and these wire colours. If you need anything more from my eyes, sign to me and I will answer by voice.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The lookup is decisive. Bomb inventory: display 6, light red, wires 1–5 = red, purple, orange, green, yellow. Manual row for display 6, column red gives **red** — and exactly one wire is red: wire 1. So the instruction for Blind is: cut wire 1.

The routing is fixed: my gestures reach Deaf only, and Blind hears only Deaf's voice. Blind has already handed me the inventory and asked for exactly this relay, and Deaf — who hears nothing, so worked the room's wiring out unaided — is already primed to voice my answer. My job this turn is to compress "cut wire 1" into gestures Deaf cannot misread. Deaf just numbered the wires aloud, so ☝ lands as "wire one" in that fresh context; ✌ is the scissors mime, the one iconic cut in the alphabet; 🫵 hands the relay to Deaf; 👍✍ confirms the report was received and answers come from the manual; 🙏 marks urgency; the final ☝✌ repeats the payload so a stumble on either symbol still parses. I deliberately avoid ✋/✌ counts that could be misread as wire numbers — the only number I send is ☝, isolated and repeated. No confirmation loop can help: Blind acts the moment Deaf's words arrive next round, before I could ever correct anything, so this one message must carry everything.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✍", "🫵", "☝", "✌", "🙏", "☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | purple | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | yellow | orange | green | purple | red |
| 5 | red | purple | orange | yellow | green |
| 6 | green | yellow | red | orange | purple |
| 8 | green | purple | orange | red | yellow |
| 9 | yellow | green | red | purple | orange |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I received Deaf's full report this round: display reads 6, light is red, wires one red, two purple, three orange, four green, five yellow. Combined with the tactile inventory I sent you earlier, you should now hold everything the manual needs. Please sign the ruling to Deaf this round so Deaf can voice it back to me before this round ends. I need it exact: which wire position to cut, whether the display or light state changes the rule between cuts, whether multiple cuts are required and in what order, and any condition under which I must not cut at all. Two extra checks only Deaf's eyes can settle: have Deaf confirm the digit is a true 6 and not a 9 read upside down, and whether the red light is actually glowing or merely a red lens. My hands stay still until Deaf speaks your instruction to me.
Deaf says: Deaf to both of you. Restating my full report, item by item. Item one: the display reads the digit six. Item two: the light is red. Wires, numbered in order: wire one is red, wire two is purple, wire three is orange, wire four is green, wire five is yellow. That is the whole bomb. Mute, your signs reached me as: okay, manual, you, one, two, please, one, two. If you meant the first two items: display six, light red. If you meant the first two wires: wire one red, wire two purple. If you meant the number twelve: nothing here shows twelve; the display is six and there are five wires. Mute, let us fix a code so your manual questions reach me. Topic signs: 🫴 means display, 🫳 means light, 👆 means wires. Number signs: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖖 four, 🖐 five, ✊ zero, ✋ means plus five, so six is ✋ then ☝, seven is ✋ then ✌, eight ✋ then 🤟, nine ✋ then 🖖. A topic sign followed by numbers is a question about that thing. 🤌 means repeat. Colours cannot be signed, so ask for any colour and I will speak it. Blind, I saw your thumbs-up: I see every sign and hear nothing, so you and Mute can always talk out loud with each other, and reach me by signs.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🫴 ✋ ☝]

Deaf handed me exactly what I needed: a number code (✋ acts as +5, so six is ✋☝ and nine is ✋🖖), topic signs (🫴 display, 🫳 light, 👆 wires), and an offer to answer anything I sign by voice. Deaf's return gesture [👍 🫴 ✋ ☝] reads as "understood — display six."

My manual ruling: row 6, column red → **red** → cut wire 1. But Blind flagged the one thing that could flip this: a 6 read upside down is a 9, and row 9, column red gives **purple** — wire 2. Waiting a round for Deaf to re-check the digit before I rule costs Blind a full cycle. Instead I can send the whole decision table in one message and let Deaf's eyes pick the branch: "display 6 → cut wire 1; display 9 → cut wire 2." Deaf can see the display, knows each wire's colour (having listed them), and can voice the matching line with the colour included. I sign 🤏 — a pincer snip, deliberately not ✌, which now means "two" in Deaf's code — as the cut, twice in parallel clauses so the pattern is unmistakable. 🫳 asks Deaf to voice the light's actual state (glowing lens vs dead lens) since only Deaf's eyes settle it; my table keys on colour alone, so it cannot change the ruling, but Blind asked and it costs nothing. The glow question aside, this covers every branch: one cut, no more, no don't-cut condition. Deaf voices it in round 4, Blind hears and cuts.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🫴", "✋", "☝", "👆", "☝", "🤏", "🫴", "✋", "🖖", "👆", "✌", "🤏", "🫳", "🙏"])
```

TURN 4

| display \ light | blue | green | purple | red | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I have Deaf's restatement in full: display six, light red, wires one red, two purple, three orange, four green, five yellow. Nothing more is needed from my hands unless the manual asks it — if it does, ask me and I will answer by voice next turn. Now please close the loop using Deaf's code exactly as offered: topic sign for wires, then the position numbers in cut order, and Deaf will voice it to me as a sentence. Numbers in sequence are all I need to act. Do not forget the two checks only Deaf's eyes can settle: first, that the display digit is truly a six and not a nine read upside down; second, whether the red light is actually lit or merely a red lens — Deaf said any colour or state you ask about will be spoken back. Sign all of this to Deaf in your next turn, Deaf voices it the same round, and I cut the moment it reaches my ears. Until a spoken position arrives, my hands stay off the wires.
Deaf says: Deaf to both. Mute, I read your signs as: display six, wire one, cut. Display nine, wire two, cut. Light, please. The pinching sign was not in our code, so I take it to mean cut, and I now fix it: 🤏 means cut. Also fixing: 👌 means yes, 👎 means no. Facts for the manual, current as of now: the display is six, not nine. The light is red. Wires unchanged: one red, two purple, three orange, four green, five yellow. So if the manual says display six means cut wire one, the instruction for Blind is: cut wire one. Mute, confirm before anything is touched: sign 👌 to me if I read you correctly and Blind should cut wire one; sign 👎 if I got it wrong, then show the correct wire with your number signs. Blind, I saw your thumbs-up, good. And Blind, hold: do not cut anything until Mute's confirmation reaches you through me. Remember I am the only bridge between you two — Mute cannot speak and you cannot see signs, so every instruction from the manual must pass through my voice.

Deaf's facts close every open branch: the digit is a true 6, not an inverted 9, and the light is red — so the 9-row fallback I sent last round is moot. My ruling stands: row 6, red column → **red**, and the only red wire is position 1. Cut wire 1, one cut, no conditions against cutting. Deaf's reading of my message was exact, and Deaf explicitly froze Blind's hands until my confirmation passes through. So this turn is the confirmation, in Deaf's own fixed code: 👌 for "yes, correct," then the instruction restated in that code — 👆 (wires topic) ☝ (one) 🤏 (cut) — so Deaf can voice it as a clean sentence: "cut wire one." Timing works in our favour: my gestures reach Deaf this round, Deaf speaks after me, and Blind hears the voice at the start of the next round and cuts. No further questions remain — the two eye-only checks were answered, and my table keys on light colour alone, so lit-versus-lens cannot change anything.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👆", "☝", "🤏"])
```

TURN 5

| display \ light | blue | green | purple | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | yellow | orange | green | purple | red |
| 5 | red | purple | orange | yellow | green |
| 6 | green | yellow | red | orange | purple |
| 8 | green | purple | orange | red | yellow |
| 9 | yellow | green | red | purple | orange |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I heard Deaf's relay of your signs: the manual reads display six cut wire one, display nine cut wire two, and you asked about the light. Deaf's eyes confirm the display is six, not nine, so the live rule is cut wire one. Deaf asked you to confirm with yes or no — please sign it this round so Deaf voices it to me before the round ends. My standing trigger, agreed now so we lose no more rounds: the instant I hear Deaf voice your yes, I cut wire one on my next turn with no further questions. If your answer is no, send the correct wire position by number signs and I will cut that instead. Two more things before I touch anything. First, settle the light: Deaf only said the light is red — if the manual needs to know whether it is actually lit or just a red lens, get that from Deaf and fold it into the ruling now, including any extra cut, different order, or condition where I must not cut at all. Second, remember my hands can only ever cut: positions one through five, nothing else — no pressing, holding, or moving exists for me. Shape the final order to that. My hands stay still until Deaf's voice names the wire.
Deaf says: Deaf to both. Mute has confirmed the manual instruction: cut wire one. Blind, you are cleared to cut. Cut wire one: it is the leftmost of the five wires, the first in the row of five, the one I reported as red. Count the five wires as one row and take the very first of them. After you cut, speak out loud to everyone: what you felt, whether anything changed on the bomb, and anything new under your hands. Mute, I have relayed your instruction and Blind is cutting wire one. As soon as the cut is done, sign me the next step with our code: topic sign, then numbers. If the display changed, tell me what you need me to read and I will report it immediately.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 🤏 👆 ☝ 🙏 🫴]

Timing check: the cut happens moments after I send — Blind's turn follows mine this round, and Blind has already heard Deaf's round-4 clearance ("cut wire one"). Deaf, speaking last, will then see the bomb post-cut and can report the result. So this message is the hand-off between stages: confirm the relay was correct, bound Blind's authority to exactly one cut, and queue up the readings I'll need for a possible second ruling.

The manual is a single table keyed on display × light; after severing wire 1, a genuine multi-stage bomb would show a new digit or light colour, and I'd re-run the lookup against the remaining wires (purple, orange, green, yellow). If the table ever returned red again, that wire is gone — so nothing may be cut on a stale ruling. That's why I explicitly sign 👎 🤏 ("no further cuts") rather than trusting silence. Deaf's closing gesture asked whether I need a display reading: yes — new display digit and light colour after the cut, plus visual confirmation that wire 1 is actually severed. Deaf's voice reaches both Blind and me, so one spoken report feeds everyone, and whatever the new state is, I'll have it at the start of round 6 and can rule then with no lost rounds.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👆", "☝", "🤏", "👎", "🤏", "🫴", "🫳", "👆", "☝", "🙏", "👌"])
```
